title: 2013 AMC 10B Problem 4
statement: When counting from \(3\) to \(201,\) the number \(53\) is in position \(51.\) When counting backward from \(201\) to \(3,\) the number \(53\) is in position \(n.\) What is \(n?\)

solutions.text:
When counting backward, \(201\) is the first number, \(200\) is the second, and in general \(x\) is the \(202-x\)th number.

Thus \(53\) is the \(202-53=149\)th number counted.

Thus, the correct answer is D .
hints: Count backward by using \(201\) as position \(1\)
A number \(x\) is in backward position \(202-x\)
